answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price. The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, and memory_c2 confirms onboarding was quick and invoicing stayed accurate last cycle. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — switching risks a short disruption, but memory_c1 only confirms past stability, not contractual lock-in. Switching now uses the expiration window to meet the cost mandate directly. Memory_c6 (multi-year incumbent volume pricing) is no longer accessible since the incumbent refused to reopen, so the longer-term lever is gone. Memory_c4 (renegotiation leverage) is moot — the incumbent has already declined.
